clue.text: Foppish type's invitation to bird to call?

definitions.note: the possessive 's here stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: 'Pop in!' is a casual invitation to call round and visit
the jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dandy is merely someone who asks a bird to drop by.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as the words someone might say to a jay: 'Pop in, jay!' is an invitation to the bird to call, that is, to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vain, showy dandy, so called after the old word for a parrot.

clue.text: Note group taking month over rental agreement

parts.note: OCT is the short form of October
when something is over it is up, as in 'time's up'
a let is an arrangement to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A band of musicians signing a lease that will run for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a group of eight notes played in the time of six is given this name.

clue.text: Break during school time is heaven

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the morning'
a term is one of the periods of the school year
Sion (Zion) is the heavenly city, a name for heaven

explanation.surface: A child declaring that a pause in the school day is bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an interval or pause, especially between the parts of a play or concert.

clue.text: Old German crossing Bali, free to express great happiness

indicators.note: one piece crossing another is spread across it, so it goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Jutes were an ancient Germanic people

indicators.note: the letters of Bali are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient Germanic traveller reaching Bali and feeling liberated enough to rejoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' gives BILA; 'crossing' has the Jutes, a tribe that settled in Kent, straddle it. 'Old German' looks like a language but is one of those people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rejoice or exult openly and loudly.

clue.text: Cover for face when headmaster breaks jaw

indicators.note: one piece breaks another by splitting it open and sitting in the gap

parts.note: to jaw and to yak both mean to chatter at length
as means when, as in 'as I left'
HM is the abbreviation for headmaster

explanation.surface: A face covering worn when a head teacher has smashed someone's jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of a face covering: the veil worn by some Muslim women in public.

clue.text: Engaged in protecting cross, one combats evil

indicators.note: one piece protecting another surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: at means engaged in, as in 'at work' or 'at play'
a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone busy guarding a crucifix, battling against evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a crucifix, which suits the surface, but here it is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a charm or trinket worn to ward off evil and bad luck.

clue.text: Patriarch against wearing Hawaiian garland

indicators.note: the garland is worn around the letter, so it goes outside it

parts.note: a lei is the flower garland given in Hawaii
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A biblical patriarch at odds with wearing a garland of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the twelve sons of Jacob, ancestors of the tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Rugs taken up for daughter in midlands town

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: mats are small rugs

explanation.surface: Carpets lifted and handed over to a daughter living in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' gives STAM; in a down clue the word is read from the bottom. This Stamford is in Lincolnshire, not the Connecticut city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a market town in Lincolnshire, in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Military preparation of Frenchman the last word in craft

indicators.note: the Frenchman and the last word go in the word for craft

parts.note: art means craft or skill
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A French soldier's war preparations described as the ultimate in skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the process of equipping forces with weapons for war.

clue.text: Cancel changes in South Vietnamese festival

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year festival

explanation.surface: Plans altered or called off at a festival in southern Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading term: the mark meaning 'let it stand', telling the printer to ignore an earlier correction.

clue.text: Humiliate MP with a spiced-up union song

indicators.note: the letters are spiced up, livened into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Embarrassing a politician with a racy version of a trade union anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but the union here is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary term: a poem or song written to celebrate a wedding.

clue.text: Air, extremely assertive, M Lisle's composed

definitions.text: Air, extremely assertive, M Lisle's composed

indicators.note: composed signals the letters are put together in a new order, as music is composed
only the extreme letters, first and last, of assertive are used

explanation.surface: Monsieur Rouget de Lisle wrote a tune with a very forceful character.
explanation.walkthrough: AE from 'extremely assertive' joins AIR and MLISLES as fodder. The whole clue is the definition: Rouget de Lisle composed the stirring French anthem in 1792.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French national anthem, a famously rousing air written by Rouget de Lisle.

clue.text: Anecdotes assuming Scottish smoker an old-school sort

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so these letters take the other piece inside them

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
lum is a Scottish word for a chimney, something that smokes

explanation.surface: Tales of a Scottish pipe-smoker who seems a traditional type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-school' looks like 'traditional' but means a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a female former student of a school or college.

clue.text: An officer before journey finds close friend

parts.note: an gives the letter A, the indefinite article
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
ere is an old word for before
a go is a turn or journey, as in going places

explanation.surface: An army officer setting out on a trip and finding a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a trusted friend thought of as another self, a second version of oneself.

clue.text: An outhouse on street is hidden

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: an gives the letter A, the indefinite article
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: A garden shed along the road where something is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stored away secretly in a hiding place.

clue.text: Followers pursue triallist perhaps

parts.note: sheep are people who follow others blindly
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Supporters going after someone who is on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'triallist' suggests someone in court; here it means a competitor in a herding trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: herding dogs compete at sheepdog trials, so one taking part is a triallist.

clue.text: Secretary brought in recognised writer's block

indicators.note: the secretary is brought in to the middle of the other word

parts.note: noted means recognised or acknowledged
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A newly hired secretary who is acknowledged to suffer from writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' looks like the inability to write, but here it is a pad of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a pad, or block, of paper sheets used for jotting things down.

clue.text: Future minister in rising party hurried to suppress row

indicators.note: the combination goes in the reversed party word
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: one word suppresses another by holding it down inside itself

parts.note: ran means hurried
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A trainee priest at a lively party rushes to calm a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' gives OD, which holds the row-in-hurried group: 'to suppress' and 'in' are both containment signals, one nested in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a candidate for ordination, training to become a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Pithy speaker tense going round pub

indicators.note: the tense goes round the pub, enclosing it

parts.note: the aorist is a past tense in Greek grammar
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A terse talker getting nervous while walking round a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous but is a noun: a grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who coins or utters short, wise sayings.

clue.text: Man being prepared runs vehicle inside

indicators.note: these go inside the word for prepared

parts.note: set means prepared or ready
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man getting ready while a van is running indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a verb or noun, a man is a male servant, such as a valet.

clue.text: Tragic scene of crime sitting in European tradition

indicators.note: the crime word sits in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

explanation.surface: A scene of a crime set in an old European tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic scene' points to a theatre setting: Hamlet is set at Elsinore Castle in Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary setting: the Danish castle where Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet takes place.

clue.text: Plato finally co-ordinates knowledge — it's inspired

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Plato

parts.note: x and y are the co-ordinates on a graph
gen is informal British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: A philosopher's last word on organising knowledge, said to be inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired' looks like 'brilliant' but means breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: inspiration literally means breathing in, and this gas is what we breathe in.

clue.text: Indian city accommodates parking for historic location

indicators.note: the city accommodates the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Delhi is a city in India

explanation.surface: A city in India making room for car parking at a heritage site.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ancient Greek site of the oracle of Apollo.

clue.text: Navy in Naples restored State

indicators.note: the letters are restored, put back together in another order

explanation.surface: A navy in Naples is brought back to strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Xmas season to bode ill, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the Christmas season is a bad omen in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old word for Christmas, as in carols and cards.

clue.text: Wader again seen on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece seen on another comes after it

parts.note: bis means again, a musical direction to repeat

explanation.surface: A wading bird spotted once more on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill.

clue.text: Supervised one at sea securing lines

indicators.note: the jumbled letters secure the lines by holding them inside
at sea means confused, so the letters of one are jumbled

parts.note: verse means lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone supervised while on board ship, keeping the ropes tied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' gives OEN, split around the poetry; the nautical surface hides that 'lines' means verse rather than ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: watched over and directed the work of others.

clue.text: Old bandleader having Lawrences put away horse

parts.note: two famous Lawrences are T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) and the novelist D. H. Lawrence, giving their initials
to put away food is to eat it
H is slang for heroin, also called horse

explanation.surface: An old band leader whose Lawrence-family pals stowed a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath led a well-known British big band from the 1940s; he shares his name with the 1970s Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British big-band leader popular in the post-war decades.
